samples.summary: Removing the `quoted` skip leaves deeply-indented / tab-indented blockquote lines unprotected, so a toggle writes a marker in front of the `>` again
samples.evidence: The old guard used `QUOTED_RE = /^\s*>/` and `replacePrefixes` skipped any matching line. The new `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` only recognises a quote after at most three *spaces*, and the `if (p.quoted) continue;` skip in `replacePrefixes` was deleted (list-commands.ts:229-237). A line such as `\t> quote` or `    > quote` (a blockquote nested inside a list item, which the editor can produce) now parses with `quote === ''`, `marker === ''`, `content === '> quote'`, and `toggleBulletList` rewrites its prefix to `indent + '- '`, producing exactly the `- > quote` corruption the previous commit's comment says it was avoiding. Nothing else guards this path: `shift`, `toggleKind` and `replacePrefixes` all now write unconditionally.

samples.summary: Quote prefixes are compared as exact strings, so a `>` without a trailing space is treated as a different block container than `> `
samples.evidence: `itemAbove`/`parentOf` do `if (prev.quote !== p.quote) return null;` and `toggleKind` keys its ordered counters on `${p.quote} ${p.indent.length}`. `QUOTE_RE` captures the optional space, so a blank quoted separator line written as `>` (the usual form — no trailing whitespace) yields `quote === '>'` while its neighbours yield `'> '`. In `> - a` / `>` / `> - b` the walk stops at the blank line, so `canIndent`/`canOutdent` are false for the third line even though it is a sibling in the same quote; likewise `>1. b` after `> 1. a` restarts ordered numbering at 1. Depth, not the literal prefix, is the right comparison.

samples.summary: `shift` applies the step computed from the topmost line to selected lines at a different quote depth
samples.evidence: `indentStep`/`outdentStep` pick `lines.find((p) => p.marker)` and `shift` then applies the same delta to every selected line. Now that quoted lines are rewritten rather than skipped, a selection spanning `- a` (plain) and `> - b` indents the quoted item too (`>   - b`), even though `itemAbove` deliberately refuses to relate the two because they are different block containers. The indent guard is per-block but the write is per-selection.

samples.summary: `taskItemText` only stops at nested UL/OL, so other nested block children are folded into the accessible name
samples.evidence: The walk breaks only on `/^(UL|OL)$/`. A task item containing a nested `<blockquote>`, `<details>` or a fenced code block after its own text still has that whole subtree's `textContent` concatenated into the `aria-label`, which is the multi-child announcement the comment says it is preventing.

finding.summary: Removing the `quoted` skip leaves deeply-indented / tab-indented blockquote lines unprotected, so a toggle writes a marker in front of the `>` again

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. QUOTE_RE at list-commands.ts:45 is /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/, so a tab-indented or 4+-space-indented blockquote line (e.g. "\t> quote", "    > quote" — a quote nested inside a two-level list) fails the quote match; parseLine (list-commands.ts:49-74) then also fails LIST_RE and yields quote='', indent='    ', marker='', content='> quote'. replacePrefixes (list-commands.ts:224-253) has no quoted-line skip, and toggleKind (list-commands.ts:263-291) computes all=false (kindOf is null) and writes prefixOf({...p, marker:'-', gap:' '}) = indent + '- ' (list-commands.ts:92-96), turning the line into "    - > quote". That is the exact corruption the repo's own test comment (list-commands.test.ts:40-45) and the ParsedLine.quote doc (list-commands.ts:20-26) say must not happen: the marker must go inside the quote. No guard exists on any path — editor.ts:581-585 and notes-toolbar.tsx:303-331 call the toggles unconditionally, and computeListState (list-commands.ts:207-217) only gates indent/outdent, not kind toggles. Reachable in normal use since indentWithTab is bound (editor.ts:369-372) and two nesting levels exceed the 3-space limit; commands.ts:278 shows the codebase elsewhere accepts /^\s*>\s?/ as a quote. Only imprecision: shift (list-commands.ts:306-312) returns prefixOf(p) unchanged for a marker-less line so it is a no-op, not a corrupting write — this does not change the verdict. Real, unguarded, wrong-output logic bug in the Correctness lane.
